mergedParams.userDescription: Split screen effect with sliding panels (divs).

output.title: Split Screen with Sliding Panel Dividers

prompts.prompt: Create a dynamic split-screen preset with sliding panel reveals, inspired by modern documentary-style editing. Think of this as two parallel video tracks that reveal themselves through animated masking. The panels should slide in from opposite directions (left panel from left, right panel from right) with a subtle overlap in the middle that creates a brief moment of compositional tension. Use a smooth ease-out curve for the slide-in (0.8s duration) followed by a gentle bounce-back effect (0.1s) to add organic movement. The panels should have a thin dividing line (2-4px) that animates in with a vertical wipe effect after the panels settle. Consider adding a subtle drop shadow on the overlapping edge to create depth. The animation should feel editorial and purposeful, like a deliberate creative choice in a high-end video production.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: Main BaseLayout container with 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden' classes containing two child BaseLayout panels with 'absolute top-0 h-full w-1/2' base classes. Left panel uses 'left-0' with initial translateX(-100%), right panel uses 'right-0' with initial translateX(100%). Apply clip-path for clean edges during animation. Use generic effects array with opacity and transform keyframes - AnimationRange from 0-0.8 for main slide with ease-out, 0.8-0.9 for subtle bounce-back. Center divider as separate BaseLayout with 'absolute left-1/2 top-0 bottom-0 w-1 bg-white/20 -translate-x-1/2 z-10' classes, using scaleY animation from 0 to 1. Each panel should contain VideoAtom or ImageAtom with fit='cover'. Consider using internal effect preset for the slide-in animation if reusability is needed. Performance: Use transform and clip-path for GPU acceleration, avoid animating width/left/right properties directly.

prompts.prompt: Design a glitch-inspired split screen where panels don't just slide but 'tear' into view with digital distortion effects. Imagine corrupted video data reassembling itself - the left and right panels should flicker into existence with rapid opacity fluctuations (3-4 quick flashes over 0.3s) before sliding into position. Add chromatic aberration during the slide by offsetting RGB channels slightly (red translateX +2px, blue translateX -2px on alternating frames). The dividing line should pulse with a data-stream effect, varying its opacity and width rhythmically. This mimics the aesthetic of cyberpunk video editing where technical glitches become artistic choices. The overall timing should feel urgent and digital - sharp ease-in curves for the initial appearance, then linear movement for the slide.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Main BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full bg-black' containing two panel BaseLayouts with 'absolute h-full w-1/2 mix-blend-screen' for glitch blending. Use complex effects array: opacity keyframes [0,1,0,1,0,1] over 0-0.3 range for flicker, combined with translateX animation. Create RGB split using three duplicate layers per panel with 'absolute inset-0' and CSS filters - filter: 'hue-rotate(120deg)' for red channel, 'hue-rotate(240deg)' for blue. Animate these with slight translateX offsets. Center divider uses AnimationRange for width (2px to 6px) and opacity (0.3 to 1) in repeating pattern. Consider using ShapeAtom for the divider with animated strokeWidth. Performance: Limit filter usage to transition period only, remove after settle. Use will-change: 'transform, opacity' during animation phase.

prompts.prompt: Build an elegant panel-slide preset inspired by premium broadcast graphics packages. The split should reveal like automated studio doors - panels slide in with perfectly synchronized timing but with a subtle mechanical delay between them (right panel starts 0.15s after left). Add a sophisticated ease-in-out-back easing that creates a slight overshoot and settle effect, mimicking hydraulic door mechanisms. Include thin accent lines that trace the panel edges during movement, leaving light trails that fade out. The composition should breathe with negative space - consider adding 20-40px gaps between panels that reveal a blurred background layer. This creates the layered depth seen in high-end motion graphics packages.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout container with 'relative w-full h-full' containing background layer (BaseLayout with 'absolute inset-0' + ImageAtom with blur filter), two panel containers with 'absolute h-full' using calculated widths 'w-[calc(50%-10px)]' for gap. Left panel 'left-0', right panel 'right-0'. Effects: Custom spring easing using cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55) for overshoot. Stagger timing using nested BaseLayouts with different animation delays. Light trails created with ::after pseudo-elements (or additional BaseLayouts) with 'absolute inset-0 bg-gradient-to-r from-white/20 to-transparent' and opacity fade from 0.3 to 0. Use transform: translateX() for main movement, avoid layout shifts. Add subtle box-shadow during movement: '0 0 20px rgba(255,255,255,0.1)'. Performance: Use transform3d() to force GPU layers, contain property for paint optimization.

prompts.prompt: Create a kinetic typography-driven split screen where the panels slide in triggered by beat detection or caption timing. Think of this as a music video effect where visual cuts are perfectly synced to audio. The panels should slam into place on strong beats with aggressive ease-in curves (0.2s duration), creating impact. Between beats, add subtle breathing animations - panels slightly scale (0.98 to 1.02) in a sine wave pattern. Include text overlays that slide in perpendicular to the panel movement, creating crossing motion paths. The overall effect should feel rhythmic and alive, constantly in motion even when 'settled'. Consider how a video editor would cut this to music - sharp, impactful, with sustained energy.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use audio analysis via fetcher for beat detection. Main BaseLayout with two panels, each with waveform effects targeting scale and translateX properties. Set beatSensitivity: 0.8, threshold: 0.7 for strong beat response. Panels use 'absolute h-full w-1/2' with initial translateX values. On beat detection, trigger translateX to 0 with ease-in timing. Breathing effect via continuous AnimationRange with scaleX/scaleY from 0.98 to 1.02, easing: 'ease-in-out', repeat. Text overlays using TextAtom with caption data, positioned 'absolute' with translateY animations perpendicular to panel slides. Use fitDurationTo: 'media' to sync with video duration. Consider creating internal effect preset 'beat-slam' for reusable beat-triggered slides. Performance: Batch animations to avoid layout thrashing, use CSS containment.

prompts.prompt: Develop a liquid morph split-screen where panels don't just slide but flow into place like viscous fluid. Inspired by experimental video art, the edges should appear to melt and reform. Use SVG clip-paths or CSS clip-path with animated path coordinates to create organic, curved edges that undulate during the transition. The panels should ease in with a custom spring physics simulation - starting slow, accelerating, then dampening into place with multiple oscillations. Add a displacement map effect during transition to create the illusion of refracting light through liquid. The aesthetic should feel organic and unpredictable, like practical effects filmed in-camera rather than digital animation.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout container with two panels using dynamic clip-path animations. Define clip-path as polygon with 8-10 points, animate each point independently using effects array. Initial state: 'clip-path: polygon(0 0, 0 0, 0 100%, 0 100%)', animate to 'polygon(0 0, 50% 0, 50% 100%, 0 100%)' with intermediate curved states. Use CSS custom properties for path animation control. Spring physics via multiple AnimationRange keyframes with decreasing amplitude oscillations. Displacement effect using CSS filter: 'url(#displacement-filter)' with inline SVG filter definition, or backdrop-filter with blur and contrast adjustments. Consider using LottieAtom for complex path morphing if available. Performance: Limit clip-path points for smooth animation, use transform for main movement, clip-path for edge detail only.

prompts.prompt: Engineer a cinematic letterbox-style split that slides panels vertically as well as horizontally, creating a complex multi-directional reveal. Picture this as a film editor's homage to anamorphic cinematography - panels slide in from corners (top-left and bottom-right) with complementary curved paths. The motion should follow quadratic bezier curves, creating arc movements that feel weighted and cinematic. Add film grain and subtle vignetting that intensifies during movement, then settles to a gentle presence. Include aspect ratio bars that slide in separately, framing the content with cinematic black bars. The timing should be deliberate and grand - 1.2s for main movement with a film-like 24fps stagger effect on certain frames.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Complex BaseLayout structure: main container with 'relative w-full h-full bg-black', two panels with 'absolute' positioning. Top-left panel: 'top-0 left-0 w-1/2 h-1/2' with origin-top-left, bottom-right panel: 'bottom-0 right-0 w-1/2 h-1/2' with origin-bottom-right. Animate using combined translateX and translateY in effects array, creating curved paths via different easing per axis. Letterbox bars as separate BaseLayouts with 'absolute left-0 right-0 h-[10%] bg-black' for top/bottom. Film grain via CSS: 'background-image: repeating-conic-gradient(...)' with animated opacity. Vignette using radial-gradient overlay. Frame stagger effect by adding micro-pauses in animation (stepped easing). Performance: Use transform-origin for rotation center, will-change for animated properties.

prompts.prompt: Design a recursive split-screen where panels subdivide into smaller panels that cascade in sequence. Think of this as a fractal edit pattern - the main split happens, then each panel splits again into smaller segments, creating a complex geometric reveal. Each subdivision should have decreasing animation duration (1s, 0.5s, 0.25s) and increasing delay offsets to create a ripple effect. The panels should slide with different directions based on their position in the grid - creating a checkerboard pattern of movement. Add subtle rotation during slides (±2 degrees) to break up the rigid geometry. This mimics advanced compositing techniques where multiple layers build up to create complexity from simple rules.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Nested BaseLayout structure with recursive component pattern. Main container splits into 2, each splits into 2 again (4 total), optionally continue to 8. Use repeatChildrenProps with indexed timing delays: delay = index * 0.1s. Each level uses 'grid grid-cols-2' or 'flex flex-wrap' for automatic subdivision. Individual panels: 'relative w-full h-full' with effects array containing translateX (alternating -100% and 100% based on index % 2), translateY for vertical variants, and rotate (random between -2 and 2 degrees). Use fitDurationTo: 'children' to ensure parent containers respect child timing. Create helper function for recursive panel generation. Consider sub-preset for individual panel animation. Performance: Limit recursion depth, use CSS contain: 'layout style paint' on panels.

prompts.prompt: Build a parallax split-screen where panels slide at different speeds and depths, creating a 2.5D effect. Inspired by multiplane camera techniques in animation, each panel should move as if on a different z-plane. The background panel slides slowly (1.5s), the foreground panels slide faster (0.7s), and UI elements slide fastest (0.3s). Add perspective transforms during movement to enhance the depth illusion - panels further back should have subtle scale reduction (0.95) and blur (1-2px). Include drop shadows that change intensity based on perceived depth. The composition should feel layered and dimensional, like looking through multiple glass planes sliding past each other.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Multiple BaseLayout layers with z-index stacking: background (z-0), midground (z-10), foreground (z-20), UI (z-30). Each layer contains panels with different animation durations in effects array. Background: 'absolute inset-0 scale-95' with slower translateX timing, blur filter: 'blur(2px)'. Midground: standard panels with 'w-1/2 h-full'. Foreground: slight scale-up 'scale-105' for depth. Perspective container: 'perspective-1000' on parent, panels use 'transform-style: preserve-3d'. Shadows via box-shadow with dynamic values: farther = softer/larger shadow. Use CSS custom properties for coordinated timing variables. Performance: GPU acceleration via transform3d(), limit blur to non-animating elements when possible.

prompts.prompt: Create a morphing split-screen where the dividing line itself becomes an animated element that draws the split. Instead of panels sliding, imagine a laser cutting through the frame - the dividing line animates from top to bottom (or in a custom path), and panels reveal through expanding masks following the line's path. The line should have energy effects - glowing, pulsing, with particle-like fragments breaking off. Add screen distortion near the cut line, as if the 'laser' is heating the pixels. The panels should have different content treatments - one side normal, other side with effects (desaturated, inverted, etc.) to emphasize the split. This creates a dramatic, sci-fi inspired transition that tells a story through its execution.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Central dividing line as primary element: ShapeAtom or BaseLayout with 'absolute left-1/2 w-1 -translate-x-1/2' and height animating from 0 to 100%. Glow effect via box-shadow: '0 0 20px rgba(0,255,255,0.8), 0 0 40px rgba(0,255,255,0.4)'. Panels use clip-path or mask-image tied to line position: 'clip-path: inset(0 50% 0 0)' animating based on line progress. Distortion via CSS filters on narrow strips near the line: multiple thin BaseLayouts with 'absolute h-full w-4' positioned along the cut, each with filter: 'blur(Xpx) brightness(1.2)' where X decreases with distance. Particle effects via multiple small BaseLayouts or ::before/::after with animated transforms. Different panel treatments via CSS filters or mix-blend-modes. Performance: Throttle particle count, use CSS animations where possible instead of JS-driven updates.

prompts.prompt: Develop a responsive split-screen that adapts its sliding behavior based on aspect ratio and screen size. In landscape, panels slide horizontally; in portrait, they slide vertically; in square formats, they use a diagonal slide. The animation should include intelligent easing that adjusts based on travel distance - longer distances use more aggressive easing curves. Add responsive typography that scales with panel size, and dynamic gaps that breathe based on available space. Include touch-gesture hints (swipe indicators) that appear briefly before the auto-animation begins. This creates an editorial piece that feels native to any viewing format, like a responsive video edit that adapts to its container.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Container queries or aspect-ratio detection via containerProps.style. Use conditional logic in presetExecution to determine slide direction. Landscape: standard horizontal translateX. Portrait: translateY with 'h-1/2 w-full' panels. Square: both translateX and translateY at 45-degree angle. Dynamic easing calculation: distance > 500px ? 'cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.46, 0.45, 0.94)' : 'ease-out'. Responsive typography via TextAtom with calculated fontSize based on container width: 'clamp(1rem, 4vw, 3rem)'. Dynamic gaps using CSS calc: 'gap-[max(1rem,2vw)]'. Swipe indicators as animated BaseLayouts with 'absolute' positioning, opacity fade 1 to 0 over 0.5s, translateX animation for swipe motion. Include aria-labels for accessibility. Performance: Use ResizeObserver for container monitoring, debounce recalculations.
